order: Add a sizing, cadence and verification protocol built from telemetry on well-sized, oversized and mega-bundle orders, optimizing effectiveness and wall-clock time while cost stays structural. In the protocol document, add a new section eight covering three parts — a sizing gate at planning, split triggers, fan-out chains and refuse-to-emit self-validation for authored tools. It covers cadence for long orders with heartbeats and checkpoint commits as externalized memory plus warm resume. The verification tax comes third, cutting rounds rather than depth. Extend the laws with pipelined recon plus CHECKPOINT as a scale escalation, then tighten review so finished work is never deferred to batch with fixes. Give the executor plus specialist templates the heartbeat plus CHECKPOINT rules, plus a rule against under-running the declared tier, then add a full or inert tier to the review runner, where inert is a claim the reviewer verifies from the diff, and unknown values resolve to full, but the launcher passes inert only when declared.
claims: The protocol section, the law and review-phase extensions, the executor and specialist rules, and the tiered runner are all in place. The tier is stamped into the engine header, and the optional verification manifest is carried into the reviewer's brief. A check-mode run clears the installer and both of its supporting scripts, and the runner's usage output shows the new tier option, full or inert. The repository carries no test suite at this point, so those 2 checks and the usage probe are the verification this surface allows.
